run.question: How does hooks/lesson-append.sh mint a lesson id (L-NNNN, highest plus one) and append the event line today, what calls it, and what breaks if the id step and the append that follows it run under a folder lock made with mkdir beside the ledger, following adapters/build-gate/maven/maven-lock.sh (mkdir as the lock, an atomic mv to take over a stale lock, a trap that frees the lock on exit)? Premise: The lesson lock reads its age with GNU stat -c %Y, else BSD stat -f %m, never takes over a lock of unreadable age, and waits at most 30 s. Premise: Until every session reloads, an old installed copy may mint a duplicate lesson id; the digest merges duplicates, and no migration is needed. Premise: The lock folder shares the ledger's ignored folder; a walker that meets it during release fails 1 gate run, which does not block.

claims.text: maven-lock.sh:34 can take over a live lock: when stat -c %Y fails, || echo 0 makes the age the whole epoch, about 1.79e9 s, above the 1800 s threshold (:35). Scripted step by step, a holder released between a waiter's -d test (:33) and its stat (:34), a third appender took the lock, and the waiter renamed that live lock away (:37) and entered as well, leaving two appenders inside. Where stat has no -c, every age read fails: with the line copied verbatim and a simulated BSD stat, 8 parallel appends made 18 and 23 take-overs and printed only 4 distinct ids in each of 2 trials. On this host's GNU stat the line fired once in 3 trials, its rename failing.

Given the premise that the lesson lock reads its age with GNU stat -c %Y, else BSD stat -f %m, and never takes over a lock of unreadable age, an unreadable age no longer lets a waiter take over a live lock: in the interleaving where maven-lock.sh:34 stole a live lock, the premise reader found the age unreadable and slept, and the third appender kept the lock; under a simulated BSD stat the premise lock printed 8 distinct ids in 2 of 2 trials. The reader has to test stat's exit status and that the value is all digits, because GNU stat -f %m exits 1 and prints file-system text. maven-lock.sh:34 keeps its own defect; the change does not touch that file.

Under the premise reader too, a stale lock can let two appenders in: two waiters both judged a 2 h old lock stale; the first renamed it to its grave and re-created the lock, and the second then renamed that fresh lock to its own grave and entered as well. maven-lock.sh:12-14 claims only one of two such contenders wins; the rename is atomic per folder, but the second rename hits the folder the winner re-created.

Measured on a prototype of the premise lock applied to a copy of hooks/lesson-append.sh: with maven-lock.sh's 10 s poll and a 30 s cap, 8 parallel appends wrote 4 unique ids and the other 4 gave up with exit 0, empty stdout and the stderr note 'nothing written', in each of 3 trials taking 34.2-35.0 s; with a 0.2 s poll all 8 were written with unique ids in 3 of 3 trials taking 11.4-12.9 s; maven-lock.sh's own age line at a 0.2 s poll also wrote 8 of 8. A solo minting append takes 642-888 ms, a python pass about 146 ms of it.

Given the premise that the lesson lock waits at most 30 s, its poll interval decides how many captures a burst of parallel appends drops: 4 of 8 at maven-lock.sh's 10 s poll, none at 0.2 s. A dropped capture exits 0 with no id, so the capturing step never notices. Neither the settled decision S-203 (docs/afk/agent-team-topology/GRILL-LOG.md:555), nor its SDD draft cell, nor the premise states a poll interval; copying maven-lock.sh:47's 10 s drops captures.

providers/CONFORMANCE.md:330 states for Claude: a command past 120 s moves to the background and is not killed; closing an agent pane sends no EXIT, TERM, INT or HUP and the command runs to its normal end, where EXIT fires; closing a plain PowerShell pane kills the process with no trappable signal. On the prototype, a held fresh lock made an append wait 32.1 s, then exit 0 with empty stdout and nothing written; a holder killed with SIGKILL (exit 137) left the lock behind, and the next append waited 31.9 s and wrote nothing, a take-over needing an age above 1800 s; a bail inside the lock exited 0 and freed the lock.

Given the premise that the lesson lock waits at most 30 s: a waiting append stays inside Claude's 120 s foreground limit, so it is never moved to the background; closing an agent pane mid-append frees the lock when the command reaches its normal end; closing a plain shell pane while an append holds the lock strands it, after which every minting append waits 30 s and writes nothing until the lock is older than 1800 s (maven-lock.sh:35). The exposure is the time inside the lock, part of a 642-888 ms solo append.
For Codex, the run-time limit of a capture command and the signals a pane close sends are unproven: providers/CONFORMANCE.md:330 records unproven, no shell.

The lock has to keep the appender's contract: write nothing to stdout, because callers take stdout as the id (skills/afk/lessons/CAPTURE.md:92; scripts/tests/test_lesson_filing.py:109-115), as maven-lock.sh:44 writes its note to stderr; give up through acquire || bail, so the script still exits 0 with a stderr note (hooks/lesson-append.sh:15-16, :23); take the lock path from the resolved ledger path (:50-54), not the working directory as maven-lock.sh:22 does: every worktree appends to the main checkout's ledger (:51-53), so a lock relative to each worktree would not exclude an appender in another worktree, and the tests relocate the ledger (scripts/tests/test_lesson_filing.py:98-99); and create the ledger folder before the first mkdir, because :73 creates it only after the mint (maven-lock.sh:30 does the same for its parent).

TERM and INT traps that release the lock and exit 143 and 130, as maven-lock.sh:64-65 do, end the script with the codes bash's default handling gives at HEAD, where hooks/lesson-append.sh sets no trap.

If the lock reads an upper-case setting that hooks/ never plainly assigns, an inline ${NAME:-default} or a self-default NAME=${NAME:-default} as maven-lock.sh:22 does for MAVEN_LOCK_DIR, check C of hooks/skill-registry-gate.sh reads every hooks/*.sh (:149), counts it as an external read (:139-140, :165-176) and blocks the Stop in the plugin's own checkout (:222, :237; hooks/stop-gates.sh:125) until skills/afk/setup/MANIFEST.md carries an E-table row for it, as it does for MAVEN_LOCK_DIR (:696) and AFK_MAVEN_LOCK_WAIT (:697).

By default scripts/create-worktree copies the main checkout's .claude into each new worktree (scripts/afk-config.py:75; scripts/create-worktree:79, :163, :201, :284-292): find lists every file (:253), then each is copied with cp (:239) under set -eE and an ERR trap (:59, :64-65). The create-worktree failure needs a file inside the lock folder: maven-lock.sh:50 writes an owner file that :17 calls forensic only, and an empty folder copied cleanly. It is not the premise's one failed gate run: create-worktree is not a gate, and the worktree that git worktree add already made (scripts/create-worktree:267-282) stays behind, so a retry under the same name is refused at :186.
